content.overview: Section 46 provides that a certificate issued under the common seal, if any, of the company or signed by two directors or by a director and the company secretary, specifying the shares held by any person, is prima facie evidence of the title of the person to such shares. The section also addresses duplicate certificates and prescribed manner and form.
content.glance: Share certificate is prima facie evidence of title; issued under seal or signed as prescribed; duplicate certificates on conditions; prescribed form and manner.
content.study: A certificate, issued under the common seal, if any, of the company or signed by two directors or by a director and the company secretary, specifying the shares held by any person, shall be prima facie evidence of the title of the person to such shares. Where a share is held in depository form, the record of the depository is the prima facie evidence. A duplicate certificate may be issued if the original is proved to have been lost or destroyed, or when the original is defaced, mutilated or torn and is surrendered, on payment of such fee and on such terms as to evidence and indemnity as the Board thinks fit. Certificates must be issued in the prescribed form and manner. Current-law framing: identify the certificate or depository record; apply the prima facie evidence rule; address duplicates and formalities.

sections.heading: Prima Facie Evidence
sections.body: A duly issued share certificate is prima facie evidence of the title of the person named to the shares specified.

sections.heading: Manner of Issue
sections.body: Issued under the common seal, if any, or signed by two directors or by a director and the company secretary, in the prescribed form and manner.

sections.heading: Demat Record
sections.body: Where shares are held in a depository, the depository’s record is the prima facie evidence of title.

sections.heading: Duplicate Certificates
sections.body: Duplicates may be issued if the original is lost, destroyed, defaced, mutilated or torn (and surrendered where applicable), on payment of fee and on terms as to evidence and indemnity as the Board thinks fit.

examples.title: Valid certificate
examples.body: A certificate signed by two directors specifying the member’s shares is prima facie evidence of that member’s title under s. 46.

examples.title: Lost certificate
examples.body: A member proves loss of the original certificate and seeks a duplicate. The Board may issue a duplicate on terms as to evidence, indemnity and fee.

hypotheticals.question: Is a share certificate conclusive evidence of title?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 46 makes it prima facie evidence only; it can be displaced by contrary proof.

hypotheticals.question: What is the evidence of title for demat shares?
hypotheticals.analysis: The record of the depository is the prima facie evidence.

distinctions.title: Certificate of shares (s. 46) vs numbering of shares (s. 45)

misconceptions.trap: A share certificate is conclusive and cannot be challenged.
misconceptions.correction: Section 46 makes it only prima facie evidence of title.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 46 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify certificate or demat record. II. Apply prima facie evidence rule. III. Address duplicates/formalities if relevant. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Certificate authenticity; prima facie title; any challenge; duplicate conditions if claimed; precise relief.

examTips: Mention demat record and duplicate rules.
